text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.1% today as oil prices dropped for a fifth consecutive day on mounting hopes for a U.S.-Iran diplomatic resolution. Reports that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if the U.S. eases military pressure, combined with Trump administration statements about ongoing talks, shifted market sentiment away from the supply-disruption fears that had driven oil and refiner stocks higher earlier this month. With crude down sharply, refiners face lower margins on the fuel they produce.

The broader backdrop adds uncertainty: while refineries are running at near-peak capacity (96.8%) and diesel storage remains relatively tight, the Trump administration is also examining a potential diesel export ban to address high fuel costs ahead of the midterms. For a refiner, that combination—lower crude prices reducing profit per gallon, plus the possibility of export restrictions limiting where they can sell—creates real headwinds regardless of how much oil they can process.
